purpose: Turn Phase 1 from a concept into a real experimental package. Per CEO R279: 'enzyme → concentration → CSF matrix → stability endpoint → catalytic endpoint → toxicity/compatibility endpoint → acceptance threshold.'
constitutional_basis: Article XXXIV — reality is the next bottleneck. Article XXVII — every threshold has provenance.
phase_1_question: Which enzyme actually works in CSF?

candidates.name: Neprilysin (NEP)
candidates.source: Recombinant human NEP (R&D Systems, catalog 1182-ZN-010 or equivalent)
candidates.rationale: Best-characterized Aβ-degrading enzyme. Decades of literature. Commercially available.

candidates.name: Insulin-degrading enzyme (IDE)
candidates.source: Recombinant human IDE (R&D Systems or Abcam)
candidates.rationale: Alternative Aβ-degrading enzyme. Broader substrate specificity.

candidates.name: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9)
candidates.rationale: Degrades Aβ in vitro. More stable as recombinant protein than NEP.

step_1_enzyme_selection.selection_criteria: All 3 candidates tested in parallel. No down-selection until data is in.

step_2_concentration_determination.method: Pilot dose-response curve for each enzyme in synthetic CSF at baseline (t=0)
step_2_concentration_determination.assay: Aβ42 ELISA (Invitrogen Aβ42 Human ELISA Kit or equivalent) — measure remaining Aβ42 after 1-hour incubation at 37°C
step_2_concentration_determination.output: EC50 and Vmax for each enzyme in synthetic CSF
step_2_concentration_determination.selected_concentration_for_stability_tes: EC80 (80% of maximal activity) — ensures we're in the sensitive range, not saturated

recipe.storage: Fresh preparation every 7 days. Stored at 4°C.

quality_control: Sterility check: plate 100 μL on blood agar, incubate 48h at 37°C, no growth
step_3_csf_matrix_preparation.rationale: Mimics human CSF ionic strength, protein content, pH, and temperature. BSA represents the dominant CSF protein (albumin). Glucose and lactate are physiological CSF metabolites.

step_4_stability_endpoint.method: 30-day incubation at 37°C in synthetic CSF. Daily activity assay.
step_4_stability_endpoint.setup: For each enzyme × selected concentration (from step 2): prepare 30 aliquots of 1 mL each in sterile glass vials. Incubate at 37°C in temperature-controlled incubator.
daily_assay_days_1_30: Add Aβ42 to 100 nM final concentration
step_4_stability_endpoint.output: Activity retention curve (30 data points) for each enzyme
step_4_stability_endpoint.threshold_provenance: MODEL_DERIVED (Article XXVII). 50% is the minimum for a clinically meaningful enzyme membrane. If the enzyme loses >50% in 30 days, the 5-year target is hopeless. This is a go/no-go gate, not a performance target.

step_5_catalytic_endpoint.method: Michaelis-Menten kinetics on the winning enzyme from step 4 (if any)
step_5_catalytic_endpoint.setup: Prepare 12 substrate concentrations: 10 nM, 30 nM, 100 nM, 300 nM, 1 μM, 3 μM, 10 μM, 30 μM, 100 μM, 300 μM, 1 mM, 3 mM
step_5_catalytic_endpoint.assay: For each concentration: incubate enzyme with Aβ42 for 5 min, 15 min, 30 min, 60 min. Measure initial rate (V0) by ELISA.
step_5_catalytic_endpoint.output: Km, Vmax, kcat for the enzyme in synthetic CSF
step_5_catalytic_endpoint.critical_interpretation: Compare measured Km to CSF Aβ42 concentration (0.1-0.2 nM). If Km >> CSF Aβ42 (expected), the enzyme operates in the linear regime — mass transport is rate-limiting, not catalysis. This REVERSES the original design intuition (enzyme loading is NOT the bottleneck; membrane geometry IS).
step_5_catalytic_endpoint.acceptance_threshold: kcat >= 1 s^-1 (sufficiently fast to clear meaningful Aβ per pass)
step_5_catalytic_endpoint.threshold_provenance: MODEL_DERIVED. At kcat=1 s^-1, with 1 μM enzyme loading and 5-second contact time, clearance per pass = 1 - exp(-1 × 1 × 5) = 99.3%. Sufficient. Below kcat=0.1 s^-1, clearance per pass drops below 50% — marginal.

step_6_toxicity_compatibility_endpoint.method: In vitro cytotoxicity and hemocompatibility screening

tests.name: Cytotoxicity (ISO 10993-5)
tests.method: L929 mouse fibroblast cell line. Expose to enzyme at 1x, 10x, 100x selected concentration for 24, 48, 72 hours. Measure viability (MTT assay).
tests.rationale: If the enzyme is toxic to fibroblasts at 10x the therapeutic concentration, it will not be safe in CSF.

tests.name: Hemocompatibility (ISO 10993-4)
tests.method: Human whole blood. Expose to enzyme at 1x concentration for 4 hours. Measure hemolysis, platelet activation, complement activation.
tests.acceptance_threshold: Hemolysis < 5%, platelet activation < 2x baseline, complement C3a < 2x baseline
tests.rationale: If the enzyme enters systemic circulation (possible via arachnoid granulations), it must not cause hemolysis or complement activation.

tests.name: CSF cell compatibility
tests.method: Human astrocytes and microglia (primary cultures or iPSC-derived). Expose to enzyme at 1x, 10x concentration for 48 hours. Measure viability and inflammatory markers (IL-6, TNF-α by ELISA).
tests.rationale: CSF-resident cells must tolerate the enzyme at therapeutic concentrations.

go_criteria: kcat >= 1 s^-1 for the winning enzyme (step 5)
CSF cell compatibility: >= 80% viability, inflammatory markers < 2x baseline (step 6)
step_7_acceptance_threshold.no_go_action: If ANY criterion fails, P-04 Phase 1 is NO-GO. The failing enzyme is recorded in the cemetery with the specific failure mode. If ALL 3 enzymes fail, P-04 as a whole is NO-GO.
step_7_acceptance_threshold.decision_logic: ALL criteria must pass for GO. Partial pass (e.g., stability OK but toxicity fails) is still NO-GO. The enzyme must be stable AND catalytically active AND biocompatible.

experimental_logistics.cost_usd: 40K-80K (enzymes $5K, ELISA kits $10K, cell culture $10K, incubator/lab space $5K, personnel $10-50K)
experimental_logistics.personnel_required: 1 biochemist (FTE, 3 months) + 1 cell biologist (0.5 FTE, 1 month for step 6)
experimental_logistics.data_management: All raw data (ELISA OD values, cell counts, pH measurements) stored in structured JSON format. Provenance: date, technician, reagent lot numbers, equipment calibration dates.

what_happens_after_phase_1.if_GO: Proceed to Phase 2 (immobilization). Winning enzyme identity, concentration, Km, kcat, and biocompatibility profile are frozen. Phase 2 tests whether the enzyme remains active when immobilized on a membrane.
what_happens_after_phase_1.if_NO_GO: P-04 enters cemetery. The finding ('no commercially available enzyme survives 30 days in CSF' or 'all candidates are cytotoxic') is a negative result that informs future enzyme selection.
